title: Stochastic Expiry + Prefix Coordination for Continuous Batching KV Eviction
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: design, implement, and validate a KV cache eviction mechanism that combines stochastic expiry (to avoid pathological synchronized expirations) with a lightweight inter-prefix coordination protocol to preserve correctness (prefix affinity) under continuous batching and GPU memory compaction. The design should minimize additional metadata per cache entry, be compatible with prefix pinning for active inferences, and provide deterministic safety properties for inflight request correctness and prefix-scoped linearizability.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Storage and Serving runtime leads
Implementation behind a runtime feature flag with unit and integration tests
Deterministic correctness invariants codified and validated via fuzzing and simulation harness
Benchmark: <5% end-to-end tail-latency regression at 99th percentile under mixed workloads compared to baseline
Metric: cache hit-rate and effective GPU memory utilization reports available in Console for rollout monitoring
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback hook defined in Console rollout configuration
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Scoped spike to identify failure modes of synchronous TTL drains under continuous batching; observed synchronized demotions causing 2x token latency spikes in worst-case synthetic workload.
2025-02-21: Proposed 'stochastic expiry' where each entry receives a small random jitter on TTL expiry to reduce correlated churn; sketched metadata layout (8-bit jitter + 16-bit lease stamp).

2025-02-24: Added prefix coordination protocol draft: lightweight lease stamping per prefix to ensure that prefetched/pinned prefixes are not evicted mid-inference. Draft includes fallbacks for cross-shard requests.

2025-02-28: Implemented prototype in local runtime branch (pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147) with unit tests for race conditions; early microbenchmarks show reduced eviction storms but minor memory overhead (~1.6%).

2025-03-04: Integration runs with continuous batching enabled; discovered edge case where long-running streaming responses can outlive TTL+stochastic window and lose a pinned prefix — added 'grace window' extension on active leases to mitigate.
2025-03-07: Started fuzz testing harness and documented canonical invariants; readying canary plan and dashboard tiles for cache telemetry.
decisions: Use stochastic expiry (per-entry TTL + small random jitter up to 10% of TTL) to avoid synchronized bulk reclamation.
Maintain a compact per-prefix 'lease stamp' (16-bit) to coordinate evictions and detect inflight usage without heavy locks.
On eviction, perform double-check against active lease stamps and recent prefix access logs to avoid reclaiming actively used prefix segments.
Keep eviction policy hybrid: base LRU/TTL scoring with prefix-affinity multiplier (score += prefix_penalty) rather than replacing LRU entirely.
Expose feature behind runtime flag 'kv.stochastic_prefix_eviction' for staged rollout and quick rollback.
risks: Increased per-entry metadata may marginally reduce effective cache capacity; must quantify memory overhead across model shard sizes.
If jitter is too small, eviction storms may persist; if too large, cold entries may linger and reduce hit rate.
Mesh between continuous batching and lease checks could add small CPU overhead on hot paths; need micro-optimizations in kernel selection.
Complexity in cross-shard requests where a prefix spans multiple GPU partitions; coordination must remain bounded and non-blocking.
dependencies: ENG-314159: update tracing hooks to propagate prefix lease stamps across RPC boundaries
ENG-121010: GPU slab allocator change that exposes fragmentation metrics to runtime
PM-404: include new KV metrics on Console rollout dashboard
test_plan: Unit tests: eviction scoring, jitter distribution, lease-stamp compare semantics
Integration tests: continuous batching enabled with mixed short/long sequence workloads; verify no prefix lost mid-inference
Simulation: deterministic replay harness to assert prefix-linearizability invariants across 1M simulated requests
Fuzzing: randomized TTL/jitter/lease timing to find race windows
Canary: rollout to 10% of traffic with extended logging and automated rollback on key metrics regression
monitoring_and_alerts: New metrics: kv.eviction.count, kv.eviction.by_reason, kv.lease_conflicts, kv.storm_detected
SLO guardrails: alert if kv.eviction.by_reason['prefix_conflict'] > 0.1% of total evictions over 5 minutes
Automated mitigation: toggle runtime flag and redirect traffic to compatible model variant on rollback
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start disabled in runtime images
Stage 1 (dev): run on Canary infra with synthetic workload for 48h
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 10% production with verbose telemetry for 72h
Stage 3 (ramp): 50% for 48h if no regressions, then 100%
Emergency rollback: runtime flag + console-based policy to revert routing to baseline model variant
open_questions: Optimal jitter distribution (uniform vs. exponential) — simulator to compare effect on eviction storm probability
Trade-off point for per-entry metadata size vs. effective cache capacity across 16GB, 32GB, 80GB GPU types
Cross-shard prefix coordination semantics: should we prefer local best-effort or global consensus for lease stamps?
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on correctness invariants in the design doc and the simulation harness coverage
Look for possible deadlocks or blocking points in the prefix coordination path under high continuous-batching pressure
Verify that the per-entry metadata layout is compact and aligned for SIMD-friendly scanning
